articles.title: DashFuel Receives Growth Investment From Five Elms Capital To Expand Petroleum Distribution Software Platform
articles.snippet:
DashFuel, a cloud-native software platform serving petroleum wholesalers, carriers, and retailers, has received a growth investment from Five Elms Capital. The funding will support the company's product development, artificial intelligence capabilities, go-to-market expansion, and customer success initiatives as it scales its operations across the petroleum distribution industry.
The post DashFuel Receives Growth Investment From Five Elms Capital To Expand Petroleum Distribution Software Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
DashFuel Receives Growth Investment From Five Elms Capital To Expand Petroleum Distribution Software Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
DashFuel Receives Growth Investment From Five Elms Capital To Expand Petroleum Distribution Software Platform
DashFuel, a cloud-native software platform serving petroleum wholesalers, carriers, and retailers, has received a growth investment from Five Elms Capital. The funding will support the company’s product development, artificial intelligence capabilities, go-to-market expansion, and customer success initiatives as it scales its operations across the petroleum distribution industry.
Founded in 2022, DashFuel provides an integrated operating platform designed to address the complex operational requirements of petroleum distribution. The industry faces challenges involving fluctuating fuel prices, logistics coordination, regulatory compliance, and fragmented technology systems that often require extensive manual processes.
DashFuel addresses these challenges by consolidating quoting, tank monitoring, dispatch, delivery, billing, reconciliation, and back-office integration into a single platform. Its technology enables petroleum operators to improve operational visibility, automate workflows, reduce administrative burdens, and protect margins while supporting business growth.
The company has established a growing customer base across the United States and reports strong gross and net revenue retention. Its platform is designed to help wholesalers and carriers expand operations without proportionally increasing headcount, while maintaining control over critical business processes.
The investment from Five Elms Capital will enable DashFuel to accelerate development of its core platform, particularly through additional AI-powered automation and workflow intelligence capabilities. These investments are intended to help customers make faster operational decisions, reduce manual intervention, and improve efficiency across petroleum distribution activities.
DashFuel also plans to expand its sales and go-to-market organization to reach additional petroleum distributors and transportation operators. Alongside these efforts, the company will continue investing in customer success and support infrastructure to maintain service quality as its customer base grows.
Five Elms Capital specializes in growth investments in business-to-business software companies, particularly those delivering AI-powered solutions for specialized industries. The firm manages more than $3 billion in assets, employs over 80 professionals, and has invested in more than 70 software platforms worldwide.
Through the partnership, Five Elms will provide capital and operational expertise to support DashFuel’s growth strategy, product innovation, customer retention, and market expansion.
KEY QUOTES:
“Petroleum distribution runs on thin margins and moves fast, prices shift multiple times a day, and a single operational miss can cost thousands of dollars and a customer relationship. We built DashFuel to give operators the infrastructure to compete: real-time visibility, intelligent automation, and end-to-end workflow control that the industry has long needed. This investment lets us build faster and reach more of the market that needs it.”
Miles Moen, Founder And CEO Of DashFuel

articles.title: October Capital Launches With Focus On AI Infrastructure, Physical Security, And Financial Infrastructure Services
articles.snippet:
Siris Capital has announced the formation of October Capital, a new private equity firm focused on investing in services businesses that help enterprises adopt, integrate, and scale transformative technologies.
The post October Capital Launches With Focus On AI Infrastructure, Physical Security, And Financial Infrastructure Services appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
October Capital Launches With Focus On AI Infrastructure, Physical Security, And Financial Infrastructure Services
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
October Capital Launches With Focus On AI Infrastructure, Physical Security, And Financial Infrastructure Services
Siris Capital has announced the formation of October Capital, a new private equity firm focused on investing in services businesses that help enterprises adopt, integrate, and scale transformative technologies.
October Capital is led by Frank Baker, who co-founded Siris in 2011 and will serve as CEO and Managing Partner. The firm launches with three investments already in place, including the completed acquisition of Takkion and signed acquisitions of EQ Retirement Solutions and Lenvi.
October Capital builds on a 15-year technology investment track record established at Siris. Over that period, Siris deployed more than $9.5 billion of equity capital, including more than $3 billion in services businesses. The firm said its services investments generated its strongest outcomes for investors.
October Capital will initially concentrate on three areas where its investment team has existing expertise: infrastructure supporting the AI economy, physical security technology, and financial infrastructure.
Within AI infrastructure, the firm plans to target services businesses that support the growing buildout of computing and power infrastructure required to deploy artificial intelligence at scale. In physical security, October Capital will focus on companies helping enterprises modernize systems used to address evolving threats.
The firm’s financial infrastructure strategy will target services supporting the modernization of financial markets, including businesses enabling automation, digital payments, and adoption of digital assets.
Baker leads a team of 16 investment professionals, including Managing Directors Dave Calamai and Seth Harward and Principals Kevin O’Brien and Grant Weisberg.
October Capital’s first completed platform investment is Takkion, a services provider to the energy industry that the firm believes is positioned to benefit from growing electricity demand associated with AI data center development.
The firm has also signed an agreement to acquire EQ Retirement Solutions, which provides pension programs with automation tools and digital payments infrastructure supporting more than 10 million members and approximately £10 billion in annual payments.
Its signed acquisition of Lenvi adds a provider of loan servicing platforms and AI-powered analytics used for areas including fraud detection and provisioning. Lenvi serves more than 150 lenders and supports over £100 billion of credit assets under management.
The formation of October Capital also follows the announced $4.2 billion sale of Equiniti to Bullish, a transaction intended to create a global transfer agent serving tokenized securities and digital assets.
October Capital is headquartered in West Palm Beach, Florida.
KEY QUOTES:
“Technologies such as AI and blockchain are going to reshape the global economy, but none of that promise matters until it works in the field. Services businesses bridge that gap, helping enterprises adopt and deploy these technologies at scale. It’s an enormous opportunity, and one we are well positioned to capture.”
Frank Baker, CEO And Managing Partner Of October Capital

articles.title: Lippincott To Acquire Athletics To Expand Digital And AI Brand Capabilities
articles.snippet:
Lippincott has entered into an agreement to acquire Athletics, a New York-based brand and innovation studio, expanding its capabilities across digital experiences, creative technology and AI-powered brand activation. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. The transaction is expected to close on November 2, 2026.
The post Lippincott To Acquire Athletics To Expand Digital And AI Brand Capabilities appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Lippincott To Acquire Athletics To Expand Digital And AI Brand Capabilities
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Lippincott To Acquire Athletics To Expand Digital And AI Brand Capabilities
Lippincott has entered into an agreement to acquire Athletics, a New York-based brand and innovation studio, expanding its capabilities across digital experiences, creative technology and AI-powered brand activation. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. The transaction is expected to close on November 2, 2026.
At closing, Athletics’ approximately 25 employees will join Lippincott while continuing to operate from the studio’s existing Brooklyn office.
Athletics combines branding and design with digital experiences, prototyping and creative technology.
The company has also developed Sesame, proprietary AI software used to create customized brand activation tools.
Lippincott plans to combine those capabilities with its existing strategy, design and engineering practices.
Management sees an opportunity to help clients move more quickly from defining a brand strategy to applying it across digital and physical customer experiences.
Athletics’ approach emphasizes prototyping and iterative development as part of the creative process, allowing teams to make brand concepts tangible earlier and refine them through testing.
The acquisition is intended to further integrate those capabilities with Lippincott’s global scale and strategic consulting work.
Lippincott has operated for more than 80 years and advises organizations on brand, experience and marketing strategy.
The firm sees AI and increasingly fragmented customer touchpoints as creating greater demand for brand systems that can be consistently applied across technology and experiences.
KEY QUOTES:
“Brands today must do much more than stand for something. They have to show up coherently across an increasingly complex set of experiences and technologies, while leaders simultaneously navigate the opportunities created by AI. Athletics’ focus on practicality strengthens our ability to translate ambitious ideas into tangible applications. Together, we can help our clients not only define what’s next for their brands, but build, activate and scale it.”
Michael D’Esopo, CEO of Lippincott
“Lippincott is a natural home for the next chapter of Athletics. We share a belief that the strongest creative work happens when strategy, design and technology come together from the beginning, with clients as part of the team and making as part of the thinking. Lippincott brings extraordinary depth in brand and business strategy and global scale. Combined with our studio approach, experimentation capabilities and proprietary technology, our entire leadership team believes we have an opportunity to take on bigger challenges and create greater impact for our clients.”
Jameson Proctor, CEO of Athletics

articles.title: ITpipes Secures Strategic Growth Investment From Luminate Capital Partners
articles.snippet:
ITpipes has received a strategic growth investment from Luminate Capital Partners to accelerate product development and expand its use of artificial intelligence across sewer and stormwater pipe inspection. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
The post ITpipes Secures Strategic Growth Investment From Luminate Capital Partners appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
ITpipes Secures Strategic Growth Investment From Luminate Capital Partners
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
ITpipes Secures Strategic Growth Investment From Luminate Capital Partners
ITpipes has received a strategic growth investment from Luminate Capital Partners to accelerate product development and expand its use of artificial intelligence across sewer and stormwater pipe inspection. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
ITpipes provides pipe inspection software used by more than 300 utilities, municipalities and CCTV contractors across the U.S. and Canada.
The platform is built on Esri ArcGIS and aligned with NASSCO PACP, MACP and LACP standards.
ITpipes plans to use Luminate’s investment to further develop AiDetect and broader capabilities for collecting, managing and analyzing underground infrastructure condition data.
AiDetect uses artificial intelligence to help identify defects found during pipe inspections.
ITpipes said the system achieves 97% defect-detection accuracy and reduces coding and quality assurance time by at least 50%.
Results are reviewed by NASSCO-certified experts.
The company plans to expand beyond AI-assisted defect coding toward a broader system of record that combines inspections, defect information and asset history to support maintenance planning, prioritization and capital allocation.
The investment comes as utilities face aging infrastructure and significant capital requirements.
ITpipes cited the American Society of Civil Engineers’ 2025 Report Card, which assigned U.S. wastewater infrastructure a D+ and estimated an annual capital investment gap of approximately $69 billion.
Lincoln International provided M&A advisory services to ITpipes shareholders, while Holland & Knight provided legal advice.
Kirkland & Ellis advised Luminate.
KEY QUOTES:
“For fifteen years, utilities and contractors have trusted ITpipes with the condition data behind their rehabilitation and capital decisions, and that trust is the foundation our AI is built on. AiDetect works because it’s trained on real inspection data and checked by NASSCO-certified experts, not because it’s the newest thing on the market. Partnering with Luminate lets us build faster for the cities, counties, and contractors who count on us, with the same reliability that earned their trust.”
Ned Bebawy, CEO of ITpipes
“ITpipes has earned something rare in this market: the trust of the utilities, municipalities, and contractors who depend on accurate inspection data every day. Ned and the team have paired that reputation with real product innovation, including AiDetect, and we’re excited to partner with them to build the tools their customers need, reliable, easy to use, and grounded in how the work actually gets done.”
Andrew Baldwin, Partner at Luminate Capital

articles.snippet:
HCLSoftware has agreed to acquire Robotiq.ai, adding enterprise robotic process automation capabilities to its HCL UnO Agentic platform. The transaction is expected to close in November 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed.
The post HCLSoftware To Acquire Robotiq.ai To Expand Agentic Automation Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
HCLSoftware To Acquire Robotiq.ai To Expand Agentic Automation Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
HCLSoftware To Acquire Robotiq.ai To Expand Agentic Automation Platform
HCLSoftware has agreed to acquire Robotiq.ai, adding enterprise robotic process automation capabilities to its HCL UnO Agentic platform. The transaction is expected to close in November 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed.
Zagreb, Croatia-based Robotiq.ai develops an enterprise RPA platform used by large banks, insurance companies and telecommunications providers.
HCLSoftware plans to use Robotiq.ai’s technology to extend AI-driven workflows into enterprise applications where APIs are unavailable or insufficient.
The combination is intended to allow AI systems not only to reason and orchestrate workflows but also to execute tasks within existing enterprise software environments.
Robotiq.ai’s platform includes ISO-certified security, audit logs and multiple deployment options designed for regulated and large enterprise customers.
HCL UnO Agentic is HCLSoftware’s agentic AI platform for coordinating AI agents and enterprise applications.
The acquisition is designed to connect orchestration and decision-making with robotic process execution across more complete business workflows.
KEY QUOTES:
“Enterprises are looking beyond AI experimentation toward production-scale automation that is secure, governed and reliable. Robotiq.ai strengthens HCL UnO Agentic by combining orchestration with enterprise-grade execution, helping customers confidently deploy and scale agentic AI across their operations.”
Kalyan Kumar, President of HCLSoftware
“We built Robotiq.ai on a simple belief: automation should be useful, fast to deploy, and reliable in production. Joining HCLSoftware gives our technology the enterprise reach, scale, and platform. Together with HCLSoftware, customers get automation that doesn’t stop at the task, it becomes part of an orchestrated, governed process across the entire enterprise.”
Darko Jovičić, CEO and Co-Founder of Robotiq.ai

articles.title: MOYOM Biotech Secures Financing From Cathay Capital To Expand Regenerative Aesthetics Business
articles.snippet:
MOYOM Biotech has completed a new financing round from the Cathay Consumer Co-Creation Fund to accelerate international growth of its regenerative aesthetics business. Financial terms of the financing were not disclosed.
The post MOYOM Biotech Secures Financing From Cathay Capital To Expand Regenerative Aesthetics Business appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
MOYOM Biotech Secures Financing From Cathay Capital To Expand Regenerative Aesthetics Business
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
MOYOM Biotech Secures Financing From Cathay Capital To Expand Regenerative Aesthetics Business
MOYOM Biotech has completed a new financing round from the Cathay Consumer Co-Creation Fund to accelerate international growth of its regenerative aesthetics business. Financial terms of the financing were not disclosed.
The Cathay Consumer Co-Creation Fund is managed by Cathay Capital and was jointly established by Cathay Capital, L’Oréal and the Shanghai Jing’an District Government.
The fund is focused on innovation spanning beauty, health and skin science.
Founded in 2018, MOYOM develops nanomedical biomaterials and Class III absorbable implantable medical devices, with a particular focus on calcium hydroxylapatite regenerative materials.
Its flagship brand is Aphranel, a CaHA-based regenerative aesthetics product designed to provide immediate structural support, regenerative stimulation and complete biodegradation.
MOYOM’s underlying platform includes its proprietary ACD-MT raspberry-shaped through-hole CaHA microspheres and PCD-ETT physically cross-linked CMC gel technology.
The company said those technologies are designed to combine structural performance, regenerative interaction and controlled biodegradation.
Aphranel received Class III medical device registration from China’s National Medical Products Administration in February 2025.
The product subsequently received certification under the European Union Medical Device Regulation in May 2026.
Since its commercial launch in May 2025, Aphranel has been introduced at more than 700 medical aesthetics clinics across China.
MOYOM plans to use Cathay Capital’s investment and global network to accelerate clinical translation, pursue additional regulatory approvals and expand into overseas markets.
The company also plans to continue investing in next-generation regenerative biomaterials.

articles.title: Locus Lock Raises Strategic Funding Led By Range Ventures For Software-Defined GNSS
articles.snippet:
Locus Lock has raised a strategic funding round led by Range Ventures to accelerate deployment of its software-defined GNSS technology across aerospace, defense, and autonomous systems. In-Q-Tel participated alongside Backswing Ventures, Aurelia Foundry, Techstars, Golden Seeds, Creations VC, POV Ventures and other investors.
The post Locus Lock Raises Strategic Funding Led By Range Ventures For Software-Defined GNSS appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Locus Lock Raises Strategic Funding Led By Range Ventures For Software-Defined GNSS
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Locus Lock Raises Strategic Funding Led By Range Ventures For Software-Defined GNSS
Locus Lock has raised a strategic funding round led by Range Ventures to accelerate deployment of its software-defined GNSS technology across aerospace, defense, and autonomous systems. In-Q-Tel participated alongside Backswing Ventures, Aurelia Foundry, Techstars, Golden Seeds, Creations VC, POV Ventures and other investors.
Locus Lock is developing positioning, navigation, and timing technology for environments where satellite navigation may be degraded, jammed, spoofed, or denied.
Rather than tying advanced GNSS capabilities to specialized hardware, Locus Lock runs signal processing in software on general-purpose computing infrastructure.
The architecture is designed to allow positioning capabilities to be updated as threats, missions and supported platforms change.
Locus Lock said it is already integrating its technology into platforms spanning air, ground, maritime, and space applications after years of development and field testing with aerospace and defense customers.
The new capital will support customer deployments, continued development of software-defined PNT technology, expansion of the engineering team and the launch of Leo200.
Leo200 is scheduled to launch in October 2026 as a software-defined GNSS receiver platform intended to provide a path from engineering evaluation through integration and deployment.
An Evaluation Kit will initially allow engineering teams to test the technology within their own systems.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’ve spent the past several years demonstrating Locus Lock in real-world RF environments with some of the top defense primes, putting the technology through the kinds of conditions our customers and partners face in the field. The threat is advancing at software speed, but the rest of the industry is still trying to counter it at hardware speed. Locus Lock closes that gap by bringing the adaptability of software to resilient positioning, allowing capabilities to evolve as quickly as the threats do.”
Hailey Nichols, Founder and CEO of Locus Lock
“Positioning and navigation underpin nearly every modern defense system and the threats to GPS are evolving faster than traditional receiver development cycles. A software-defined approach creates the ability to adapt positioning capabilities much more rapidly as threats, missions, and platforms change. Locus Lock is building an architecture for PNT that reflects where both the technology and the operating environment are going and aligns to the demand signal we’ve seen from the U.S. and allied nations.”
Nat Puffer, Partner at In-Q-Tel
“When networking, radio and automotive moved from purpose-built hardware to software on general-purpose compute, multi-year design cycles became release cycles measured in weeks, and entire industries were reshaped as a result. GNSS is one of the last critical technologies still tied to hardware, and it’s the one where adaptability matters most. Jamming and spoofing evolve at software speed, and new constellations and signals are coming online faster than any hardware roadmap can absorb. A receiver that has to be redesigned to keep up will always be behind. Hailey and the team have proven a software-defined architecture works in real contested environments, and we think it becomes the foundation for how every autonomous platform navigates.

articles.title: HappyCo Secures Investment From Lone View Capital To Expand AI-Powered Property Operations Platform
articles.snippet:
HappyCo has received a significant investment from Lone View Capital to accelerate development and adoption of its property operations platform for multifamily housing. The financial terms were not disclosed.
The post HappyCo Secures Investment From Lone View Capital To Expand AI-Powered Property Operations Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
HappyCo Secures Investment From Lone View Capital To Expand AI-Powered Property Operations Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
HappyCo Secures Investment From Lone View Capital To Expand AI-Powered Property Operations Platform
HappyCo has received a significant investment from Lone View Capital to accelerate development and adoption of its property operations platform for multifamily housing. The financial terms were not disclosed.
HappyCo’s existing management team, led by founder and CEO Jindou Lee, will continue leading the company following the transaction.
Founded in 2011, HappyCo began as a property inspection solution and has expanded into a broader platform spanning maintenance, asset management, and sourcing workflows.
A major part of the company’s recent development has been JoyAI, an artificial intelligence orchestration layer designed to automate and optimize operational tasks for on-site property teams.
HappyCo serves many of the largest multifamily owners and operators, including the majority of the National Multifamily Housing Council’s top 50 managers. Its products have been deployed across more than five million apartment homes.
The company has built its platform using more than a decade of maintenance interactions and data from approximately one billion inspected items.
HappyCo plans to use Lone View’s backing to continue investing in product development, AI capabilities and customer success while expanding the reach of its platform.
Houlihan Lokey served as financial adviser to HappyCo and DLA Piper served as its legal counsel. Ropes & Gray served as legal counsel to Lone View.
KEY QUOTES:
“For more than a decade, we’ve been focused on solving real operational problems for our customers. Today marks the beginning of the next chapter in that journey. Our customers consistently tell us two things: they want best-in-class software and they want products to work together seamlessly. Our partnership with Lone View will enable us to continue building exceptional products and collaborating with other great companies to deliver even more value for our customers.”
Jindou Lee, Founder and CEO of HappyCo
“We’re excited to partner with Jindou and the entire HappyCo team as they execute on the next phase of their vision. HappyCo has built a market-leading platform, earned the trust of the industry’s largest owners and operators, and established a strong foundation for future growth. We look forward to bringing our experience scaling technology businesses to help HappyCo build on their strong momentum and support their long-term growth.”
Doug Ceto, Partner at Lone View Capital

articles.title: Rising Tide Raises Seed Round Led By Left Lane Capital For AI-Powered Property Management Network
articles.snippet:
Rising Tide has closed an undisclosed seed financing led by Left Lane Capital to expand its network of independently owned residential property management companies.
The post Rising Tide Raises Seed Round Led By Left Lane Capital For AI-Powered Property Management Network appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Rising Tide Raises Seed Round Led By Left Lane Capital For AI-Powered Property Management Network
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
Rising Tide Raises Seed Round Led By Left Lane Capital For AI-Powered Property Management Network
Rising Tide has closed an undisclosed seed financing led by Left Lane Capital to expand its network of independently owned residential property management companies.
Left Lane incubated Rising Tide alongside founder and CEO Blake Mohseni based on the firms’ view that property management represents a large, fragmented market where artificial intelligence can automate administrative work without eliminating local operating relationships.
Rising Tide is building what it describes as a federation of independent property management businesses.
Rather than consolidating acquired companies under one national brand, Rising Tide provides capital and shared technology while allowing participating operators to retain their local names, teams and customer relationships.
The company is targeting a property management market it estimates exceeds $100 billion and includes more than 240,000 firms.
Rising Tide believes many smaller operators lack the technology, systems and back-office infrastructure available to larger institutional platforms.
Its strategy centers on using AI to reduce administrative workloads so local operators can spend more time working directly with property owners and tenants.
The company is developing those tools through The Lab, where Rising Tide builds and tests AI applications inside operating property management companies.
The Lab is currently working with three property management firms. Rising Tide retains ownership of the technology it develops, while participating operators receive access at no cost and retain control of their business data.
Left Lane Capital was founded in 2019 and invests in high-growth internet and consumer technology companies from offices in New York and London.
KEY QUOTES:
“AI is changing the definition of what premier service looks like in property management. It gives our operators more room for the relationships with owners and tenants that actually built their business. This funding brings that same approach to more independent property management firms: real technology, real capital, and partnership instead of a takeover.”
Blake Mohseni, Founder and CEO of Rising Tide
“We have invested over $100 million into AI companies transforming traditional services industries, from accounting to dental. Property management is universal, mission-critical, and not for the faint of heart. Blake and his team have the thoughtful approach needed to bring AI to the industry and drive modernization alongside tenured operators.”
Vinny Pujji, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Left Lane Capital
